topics: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, and its SI unit is the pascal (1 Pa = 1 N m⁻²).

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of work (or energy)?
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance = MLT⁻² × L = ML²T⁻².

questions.q: How many significant figures are there in the measurement 6.020 × 10³ kg?
questions.explanation: The digits 6, 0, 2 and the trailing 0 after the decimal point are all significant, giving 4.

questions.q: The radius of a sphere is measured with a possible error of 2%. What is the possible percentage error in its calculated volume?
questions.explanation: Volume ∝ r³, so the fractional error in V is 3 × 2% = 6%.

questions.q: From Newton's law of gravitation F = G m₁m₂ / r², what is the dimensional formula of the gravitational constant G?
questions.explanation: G = F r² / (m₁m₂) = (MLT⁻²)(L²)/M² = M⁻¹L³T⁻².

questions.q: Which pair of physical quantities has the same dimensions?
questions.explanation: Torque (force × distance) and energy both have dimensions ML²T⁻²; the other pairs differ.

questions.q: What is a light year? Is it a unit of time or of distance?
questions.answer: A light year is a unit of distance: the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year, about 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.
keyPoints: It is a unit of distance, not time
Distance travelled by light in vacuum in one year
questions.explanation: Light travels about 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, so in one year it covers roughly 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.

questions.q: A resistance is found from R = V/I, with V = (100 ± 5) V and I = (10 ± 0.2) A. Find the maximum percentage error in R.
keyPoints: For a quotient, add percentage errors: 5% + 2% = 7%
questions.explanation: In a quotient the maximum fractional errors add, so ΔR/R = 5% + 2% = 7%.

questions.q: In a position–time graph, what does the slope of the graph give?
questions.explanation: Slope of x–t graph = dx/dt, which is velocity.

questions.q: The area under a velocity–time graph between two instants gives
questions.explanation: Area under a v–t graph is the integral of v dt, which is displacement.

questions.q: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m s⁻² for 5 s. What distance does it cover in this time?
A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and ignoring air resistance, what maximum height does it reach?
A body falls freely from rest. What is the ratio of the distances covered in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd seconds?
questions.explanation: Distance in the nth second = ½g(2n−1), so the distances are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5.

questions.q: A stone dropped from the top of a tower reaches the ground after 4 s. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what distance does it cover in the last second of its fall?
questions.explanation: Height in 4 s = ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 m; in 3 s = 45 m; last second = 80 − 45 = 35 m.

questions.q: A car travelling at 72 km/h is brought to rest by uniform braking in 5 s. Find the deceleration and the stopping distance.
questions.answer: Deceleration = 4 m s⁻²; stopping distance = 50 m.
questions.explanation: Convert 72 km/h to 20 m s⁻¹, then use v = u + at and s = average speed × time.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 30 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the time of flight until it returns to the thrower's hand and the maximum height reached.
questions.answer: Time of flight = 6 s; maximum height = 45 m.
questions.explanation: The motion up and down is symmetric, so the total time is twice u/g.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; the others are scalars.

questions.q: For a given speed of projection (no air resistance, level ground), the horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is
questions.explanation: Range = u² sin 2θ / g is maximum when sin 2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the resultant of two perpendicular forces of 3 N and 4 N?
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its time of flight on level ground?
A projectile fired at 15° to the horizontal has the same horizontal range as another projectile fired with the same speed at which angle?
questions.explanation: Range depends on sin 2θ, which is equal for complementary angles θ and 90° − θ; the complement of 15° is 75°.

questions.q: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a horizontal circle at constant speed. If the string suddenly breaks, in what direction does the stone initially move (ignoring gravity for the moment of release)?
options: Along the tangent to the circle at that point
questions.explanation: With no net force, the stone continues with its instantaneous velocity, which is tangent to the circle.

questions.q: A body moves in a circle of radius 0.5 m with a constant speed of 5 m s⁻¹. Find its centripetal acceleration.
questions.answer: 50 m s⁻² directed towards the centre.
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is v²/r = 25/0.5 = 50 m s⁻².

questions.q: A ball is thrown horizontally at 15 m s⁻¹ from the top of an 80 m high cliff. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the time taken to reach the ground and the horizontal distance covered.
keyPoints: Vertical motion: 80 = ½ × 10 × t², so t = 4 s
questions.explanation: Vertical and horizontal motions are independent; the fall time fixes the horizontal distance.

questions.q: Which physical quantity is a measure of the inertia of a body?
questions.explanation: The greater the mass, the greater the inertia (resistance to change in the state of motion).

questions.q: Newton's first law of motion gives the concept of
questions.explanation: The first law states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted on by an external force; this property is inertia.

questions.q: A net force of 20 N acts on a 5 kg block. What is the acceleration of the block?
A 10 kg block rests on a horizontal surface with coefficient of static friction 0.4. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the maximum static friction force?
A 60 kg person stands on a weighing scale in a lift that accelerates upward at 2 m s⁻². Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what does the scale read (as a force)?
questions.explanation: N − mg = ma, so N = m(g + a) = 60 × 12 = 720 N.

questions.q: Blocks of 2 kg and 3 kg touch each other on a smooth horizontal table. A horizontal force of 10 N pushes the 2 kg block towards the 3 kg block. What force does the 2 kg block exert on the 3 kg block?
questions.explanation: Common acceleration = 10/5 = 2 m s⁻²; the force on the 3 kg block is 3 × 2 = 6 N.

questions.q: A bullet of mass 20 g is fired at 300 m s⁻¹ from a gun of mass 4 kg. Find the recoil speed of the gun.
keyPoints: Total momentum before firing is zero
V = 6/4 = 1.5 m s⁻¹, opposite to the bullet
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum gives the gun a momentum equal and opposite to the bullet's (6 kg m s⁻¹).

questions.q: A block just begins to slide on a rough plane when the plane is tilted to 30° with the horizontal. Find the coefficient of static friction.
keyPoints: At the point of sliding, mg sinθ = μ mg cosθ
questions.explanation: At the angle of repose the component of weight along the plane equals the limiting friction.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 J s⁻¹.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, the work done by the centripetal force is
questions.explanation: The force is perpendicular to the displacement at every instant, so W = Fs cos 90° = 0.

questions.q: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 3 m s⁻¹?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

questions.q: A force of 10 N moves a body through 5 m. The force makes an angle of 60° with the displacement. How much work does the force do?
The momentum of a body is increased by 100%. By what percentage does its kinetic energy increase?
questions.explanation: KE = p²/2m. Doubling p makes KE four times, an increase of 300%.

questions.q: A pump raises 100 kg of water through a height of 20 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the power delivered to the water?
A spring of force constant 200 N m⁻¹ is compressed by 0.1 m. Find the elastic potential energy stored.
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy of a spring is ½kx² = 0.5 × 200 × 0.01 = 1 J.

questions.q: A ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. Using energy conservation and g = 10 m s⁻², find its speed just before it hits the ground (ignore air resistance).
keyPoints: Loss of PE = gain of KE: mgh = ½mv²
v ≈ 14.1 m s⁻¹, independent of mass
questions.explanation: Equating mgh to ½mv² gives v = √200 ≈ 14.1 m s⁻¹.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of torque?
questions.explanation: Torque = force × perpendicular distance, with unit newton metre.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a rigid body depends on
options: its mass distribution and the position of the axis
questions.explanation: I = Σmr² depends on how the mass is distributed about the chosen axis.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the moment of inertia of a thin ring of mass M and radius R about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its plane?
questions.explanation: All the mass is at distance R from the axis, so I = MR².

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A force of 10 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.3 m from an axis. What is the torque about the axis?

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A spinning skater pulls her arms in. Her angular momentum is conserved. What happens to her rotational kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: KE = L²/2I; I decreases while L is fixed, so KE increases (she does internal work pulling the arms in).

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid disc and a ring of the same mass and radius roll without slipping from rest down the same incline. Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.explanation: The disc has a smaller moment of inertia, so less energy goes into rotation and it has a larger acceleration (g sinθ / (1 + k²/R²)).

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A wheel of moment of inertia 0.5 kg m² rotates at 20 rad s⁻¹. Find its angular momentum and rotational kinetic energy.
questions.answer: L = 10 kg m² s⁻¹; KE = 100 J.
questions.explanation: Use L = Iω and KE = ½Iω².

questions.q: Which scientist gave the three laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation: Johannes Kepler formulated the three laws of planetary motion.

questions.q: Kepler's second law (equal areas swept in equal times) is a consequence of conservation of
questions.explanation: The gravitational force is central, so torque about the Sun is zero and angular momentum is conserved.

questions.q: At a height equal to the radius of the Earth above its surface, the acceleration due to gravity is
questions.explanation: g' = g R²/(R + h)² = g R²/(2R)² = g/4.

questions.q: The escape speed from the Earth's surface compared with the orbital speed of a satellite just above the surface is
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2gR) and v_o = √(gR), so v_e = √2 v_o (about 11.2 km s⁻¹ versus 7.9 km s⁻¹).

questions.q: Assuming the Earth to be a uniform sphere, what is the weight of a body of mass m at the centre of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Inside a uniform sphere g falls linearly with distance from the centre and is zero at the centre.

questions.q: A satellite is moved from an orbit of radius r to one of radius 4r around the same planet. By what factor does its time period change?
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law T² ∝ r³, so T ∝ r^{3/2} = 4^{3/2} = 8 times.

questions.q: A planet has twice the mass and twice the radius of the Earth. Find its surface gravity in terms of the Earth's g.
questions.explanation: Doubling mass doubles g, doubling radius divides g by 4, so the net factor is 1/2.

questions.q: Stress is defined as
questions.explanation: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit cross-sectional area.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus = stress/strain, and strain is dimensionless, so it has the unit of stress, N m⁻² or pascal.

questions.q: A wire of original length 2 m stretches by 1 mm under a load. What is the longitudinal strain?
questions.explanation: Strain = ΔL/L = 1 × 10⁻³ m / 2 m = 5 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.q: A wire of cross-section 1 mm² and Young's modulus 2 × 10¹¹ Pa carries a tensile force of 100 N. What is the strain produced?
questions.explanation: Stress = 100 / 10⁻⁶ = 10⁸ Pa, so strain = 10⁸ / (2 × 10¹¹) = 5 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.q: Two wires of the same material and length have radii r and 2r. The same load is hung from each. What is the ratio of the extension of the thinner wire to that of the thicker wire?
questions.explanation: Extension = FL/(πr²Y) ∝ 1/r², so the ratio is (1/r²) : (1/4r²) = 4 : 1.

questions.q: The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume in a stretched wire is
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × F × ΔL, and dividing by volume AL gives ½ × (F/A) × (ΔL/L).

questions.q: A steel wire of length 3 m and cross-section 2 × 10⁻⁶ m² carries a load of 40 N. Young's modulus of steel is 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻². Find the extension.
questions.explanation: Substituting in Y = FL/(AΔL) gives ΔL = 3 × 10⁻⁴ m.

questions.q: A hydraulic lift works on the principle of
questions.explanation: Pascal's law says pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity?
questions.explanation: η = F/(A · dv/dx) has unit N s m⁻² = Pa s.

questions.q: Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and density of water 1000 kg m⁻³, what is the gauge pressure at a depth of 10 m in water?
In a hydraulic lift the large piston has 50 times the area of the small piston. A force of 100 N is applied to the small piston. What force acts on the large piston?
questions.explanation: Pressure is the same, so F₂ = F₁ × (A₂/A₁) = 100 × 50 = 5000 N.

questions.q: A block of density 600 kg m⁻³ floats in water of density 1000 kg m⁻³. What fraction of its volume is submerged?
questions.explanation: For floating, weight = buoyant force: ρ_block V = ρ_water V_sub, so V_sub/V = 0.6.

questions.q: Water flows steadily through a horizontal pipe whose radius is reduced to half. How does the flow speed in the narrow part compare with that in the wide part?
questions.explanation: Equation of continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂. Area becomes one-quarter, so the speed becomes 4 times.

questions.q: Find the excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 2 cm if the surface tension of the soap solution is 0.03 N m⁻¹.
keyPoints: A soap bubble has two surfaces, so ΔP = 4S/r
questions.explanation: Two liquid surfaces each contribute 2S/r, giving ΔP = 4S/r = 6 Pa.

questions.q: Water (surface tension 0.07 N m⁻¹, density 1000 kg m⁻³, contact angle 0°) rises in a capillary tube of radius 0.5 mm. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², find the height of the rise.
questions.explanation: Capillary rise follows h = 2S cosθ/(rρg), giving 0.028 m.

questions.q: Absolute zero on the Celsius scale is approximately
questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 K) corresponds to −273.15 °C.

questions.q: While ice melts at 0 °C, the heat supplied
options: is lost to the surroundings only
changes its state without changing its temperature
questions.explanation: The heat supplied is latent heat; it breaks the structure of the solid while the temperature stays constant.

questions.q: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 10 °C? (Specific heat of water = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
A 100 m long steel rail has α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. By how much does it expand when its temperature rises by 50 °C?
100 g of water at 80 °C is mixed with 100 g of water at 20 °C in an insulated container. What is the final temperature?
questions.explanation: With equal masses and the same specific heat, the final temperature is the average, 50 °C.

questions.q: According to Stefan–Boltzmann law, the power radiated by a black body is proportional to T⁴. If its absolute temperature is doubled, the power radiated becomes
questions.explanation: Power ∝ T⁴, so doubling T multiplies the power by 2⁴ = 16.

questions.q: How much heat is needed to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C? The latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Heat needed for a change of state is mL = 0.5 × 3.36 × 10⁵ J.

questions.q: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of conservation of
questions.explanation: It states that heat supplied to a system equals the increase in internal energy plus the work done by the system.

questions.q: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is
questions.explanation: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, which stays constant.

questions.q: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. What is the change in its internal energy?
What is the efficiency of a Carnot engine working between 600 K and 300 K?
A gas at a constant pressure of 2 × 10⁵ Pa expands from 1 litre to 3 litres (1 litre = 10⁻³ m³). How much work does it do?
An ideal gas is compressed adiabatically. What happens to its temperature?
questions.explanation: With Q = 0, the work done on the gas increases its internal energy, so its temperature rises.

questions.q: A Carnot engine has a source at 400 K and a sink at 300 K. Find its efficiency and the work done per cycle if it absorbs 1000 J from the source.
questions.explanation: Work output is the efficiency times the heat absorbed from the source.

questions.q: The number of molecules in one mole of a substance is
questions.explanation: This is Avogadro's number, 6.022 × 10²³ per mole.

questions.q: The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is directly proportional to its
questions.explanation: Average KE per molecule = (3/2)k_B T.

questions.q: How many degrees of freedom does a monatomic gas molecule have?
questions.explanation: A monatomic molecule has three translational degrees of freedom.

questions.q: If the absolute temperature of a gas is made four times, its rms speed becomes
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ √T, so quadrupling T doubles v_rms.

questions.q: At the same temperature, what is the ratio of the rms speed of hydrogen (molar mass 2 g/mol) to that of oxygen (molar mass 32 g/mol)?
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ 1/√M, so the ratio is √(32/2) = √16 = 4.

questions.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas occupy 5 litres at 300 K. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the approximate pressure?
Find the total translational kinetic energy of 1 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K. (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Translational KE of one mole is (3/2)RT = 3739.5 J.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration of the particle is directly proportional to its
questions.explanation: The defining condition of SHM is a = −ω²x.

questions.q: The frequency f and time period T of an oscillation are related by
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second, f = 1/T.

questions.q: What is the time period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m? (Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².)
A 0.5 kg mass is attached to a spring of force constant 200 N m⁻¹. What is the time period of its oscillations?
A particle executes SHM with amplitude 0.1 m and frequency 5 Hz. What is its maximum speed?
questions.explanation: ω = 2πf = 10π rad s⁻¹; v_max = Aω = 0.1 × 31.4 = 3.14 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: The length of a simple pendulum is made four times. Its time period
questions.explanation: T ∝ √l, so four times the length gives twice the time period.

questions.q: A 0.2 kg particle performs SHM with angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.05 m. Find its total mechanical energy.
questions.explanation: Total energy in SHM is ½mω²A² = 0.025 J.

questions.q: Sound waves in air are
questions.explanation: Air particles vibrate along the direction of propagation, forming compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: The speed v, frequency f and wavelength λ of a wave are related by
questions.explanation: A wave travels one wavelength in each period, so v = λ/T = fλ.

questions.q: A sound wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. What is its speed?
A string of length L fixed at both ends has a wave speed v. What is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: In the fundamental mode L = λ/2, so f = v/λ = v/2L.

questions.q: A pipe closed at one end is 0.85 m long. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, what is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe f = v/4L = 340/(4 × 0.85) = 100 Hz.

questions.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. What is the beat frequency?
questions.explanation: Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂| = 4 Hz.

questions.q: A travelling wave is described by y = 0.02 sin(10πt − πx) in SI units. Find its amplitude, frequency, wavelength and speed.
questions.answer: Amplitude 0.02 m; frequency 5 Hz; wavelength 2 m; speed 10 m s⁻¹.
keyPoints: Compare with y = A sin(ωt − kx): A = 0.02 m
ω = 10π gives f = ω/2π = 5 Hz; k = π gives λ = 2π/k = 2 m
questions.explanation: Reading A, ω and k from the equation gives f, λ and v = ω/k = 10 m s⁻¹.
